153. Kinselo's Purpose (3)
Bouvard, not knowing such a fact, kept expressing greedy admiration at the sight of the machinery and blueprints.
"Is this...engineering? Ha! Hey, unlucky lad. Do you also just think of this as engineering?"
The young man, thus addressed as Kwaul, felt somewhat flushed.
The golden thread product made Kwaul, who seemed like a bandit leader, appear as a muscular youth. His clean-shaven face seemed quite attractive.
"It's engineering."

"Fool! This is not just engineering, it's art, art! Ah, it's disgusting that such a precious work has to be entrusted to the likes of you. This complex, geometric cipher, design, no masterpiece can match it."
The complex cipher that Bouvard mentioned was all made by Kwaul, so he was receiving both insult and compliment from him at the same time.
Listening to Bouvard's exclamations, like 'Heh, ha, ho,' for three hours was a truly painful ordeal for both the Barmel Alliance and Kinselo.
Jin, as if he had barely put up with the noise all this time, immediately retrieved the items when the time came.
"Ah, it's already over!?"
"Yes, it's over, so leave."
"Can't I see it a little bit more......!"
"Take your hand off, before I cut it off."
At Jin's cold voice, Bouvard stepped back in surprise.
"Ha, ha ha! Anyway, you'll need my help to understand those artworks! Even if you beg then, I won't help!"
Bouvard was under the illusion that he had obtained quite a lot of information from the items. From Bouvard's point of view, it was indeed so.
The executives of Kinselo also suspected that they had made some gains, watching the excited Bouvard with regret.
If they hadn't realized the trap at all, they might have been suspicious. Kwaul had set it up so that Bouvard could only identify core information (from Kwaul's perspective) to a limited extent.
"Then this meeting is over."
Suddenly, Jin followed Bouvard as he turned to leave.
"No, you crazy! I put my hand away as you said, why, why are you doing this!"
Bouvard naturally thought Jin was following him with the intention of assaulting or slashing him. He was the only one who felt this way.
The rest of the group, they clearly perceived who Jin's killing intent was directed towards.
Bianca Caligo.
Caligo's first princess, Jin bypassed the stumbling Bouvard and was heading towards her.
"What's your name, demon?"
"Bianca Caligo... What... business... do you have with me?"
"I was curious about how strong one needs to be to match the left arm of the Black Knight Mon."
"Who... is that?"
An invisible hostility was ominously wavering between the two. Like a powder keg that could explode at the drop of a spark.
The first to withdraw was Jin.
"I'll let you know next time."
As Jin turned and strode back to his companions, Bianca realized that her fur had bristled at some point.
"So rude, until the end! Inferior human! Sister, you should have just blasted him!"
Ainas, who had been shrunken by the two's aura, yelled out.
If Jin had drawn his sword and started the fight just now, Bianca would have been sure of her victory, a hundred out of a hundred times.
However, an unfamiliar sense of unease came. The only moment she could win against Jin would be now.
"Archduke... Marjiella."
"Yes, Princess Caligo?"
"Wouldn't it be... better... to kill him now?"
He might become more dangerous than all of Runkandel if not now. That's what Bianca was saying.
"Hmm, it seems he won't be on our side, but I think he still has work to do for the world."
"He seems to know well that we won't kill him even if he jumps like that, Marjiella. We gave too much information to that demon."
"Demons are inherently unfair creatures, aren't they? When the angel wakes up, he will repent."
Even after Jin and his party left on the moat, Bianca couldn't take her eyes off the spot where Jin had stood for a long time.
While Jin and his colleagues were negotiating, Zet moved all his inventions that had remained in Kwaul's shack to Tikan.
"Bouvard Gaston, was it? That disgusting guy. But he's pretty impressive. I don't know about his brain, but as far as his craftsmanship is concerned, he outdid me."
Kwaul said, examining his inventions. Jin had broken a few, but most were intact. Amela's eyes shone as she looked at the inventions.

"He couldn't get the core information because of the trap, but he's the initial developer of the Mana Stone, and is suspected to be the reincarnation of the God of Pieces. He'll probably make something with the information he got this time. It seems that even the leader of those who are presumed to be unable to act externally has a special power."
"As long as their technological advancement doesn't exceed Kwaul's expectations, there won't be a big problem."

"Even if the hand is good, without the brain there's no answer. They'll quickly follow the spaceship because they already have a finished product called Grunil, but they won't even dream of the space-time device."
"They already have the ability to teleport in the form of a steel door, though."
Technologies that could change the course of war, spaceships and teleportation devices.
Now, the technological power of Runecandel, which had been far behind Ziph and Kinzel, who initially lacked even the ability and will to develop, will become equal or superior to them.
Strictly speaking, it's the technology of the Babel Union, not Runecandel.
"King of Demons, Orgal...."
While the two were talking, Quicantel recalled the leader of Kinzel.
King of Demons, Orgal, about whom Quicantel had spoken with Murakan a few times. So Quicantel was particularly confused.
"I know for sure he was betrayed by Helluram and died. Moreover, during the Colon massacre, didn't Myron try to summon Orgal from Hell and possess him?"
"I'm also curious about that part, Lord Quicantel."
To confirm Orgal's death, Jin even temporarily summoned Tess, who was in recovery, and Tess also seemed to know that he had died. Shuri, who was Helluram's enemy, was the same.
"Thinking about it, whenever a story about Orgal came up, Murakan and I naturally changed the subject. I didn't think much about him, but perhaps even that was due to historical manipulation."
"What kind of person was Orgal?"
Murakan only told him 'a great demon.' But there aren't many beings in the world that Murakan praises as great with his own mouth.
"I don't... remember in detail. But, Murakan and I didn't particularly dislike him... in some ways, we admired him."
"Admiration? Murakan?"
"Yes. Just by enduring Helluram's curse, the whole world owed him as much as anything."
"You mean, he prevented Helluram's curse from spreading in the world?"
"Yes. I remember that clearly. I don't remember him stopping either Temar or Murakan when they were out of control."
"If he was such a being, perhaps even Ziph itself didn't know that they had manipulated Orgal's history."
Then, it also explained why Myron Ziph tried to possess Orgal.
Most of all, Myron's possession black magic didn't fully unfold at the time. Jin cut off the hell gate he summoned before the magic was completed.
"Even if Ziph knew, there's a possibility that the information didn't reach Myron."

"That's a plausible story. There's too much history that has been lost or manipulated over a thousand years. I can't even consider my memory of him saving the world from Helluram as complete. Anyway, if Kinzel's goal is world purification, there are parts that resonate with the image of Orgal in my unstable memory."
Regardless of Kinzel's actual purpose, the madmen must not be allowed to hold the world's hegemony. All the comrades thought so unanimously.
In any case, to uncover the truth of history, they had no choice but to wait for Valeria's record magic to become complete and to verify the legacy of Solderet.
"When Orgal fully recovers is crucial."
Runecandel, Ziph, Kinzel. Recovery was the key for all three forces.
No one knew which force would recover first.
So, what the leaders of each force needed to do was to streamline their ranks as quickly as possible while the war was halted.
In that regard, Jin was already in the best condition. He was lucky to have acquired Kwaul from the start, and with the ceasefire agreement in place, he could focus on growth without interference.
However, Jin felt a slight anxiety because he could not be sure that he was in the most advantageous position.
"Right. But don't worry too much. The world will keep turning even while you're gone."
Quicantel knew exactly what kind of anxiety Jin, who would soon leave for Lafrarosa, was experiencing.

"It's okay if something happens to Tichan while you're gone since Runecandel's protection is now in place instead of Murakan. Besides, the Abyssal Lord is also focusing on recovery, so it won't be long before Lady Misha returns to her place. Then Murakan will return to Tichan as well. Put your mind at ease a little."
"I understand, Lord Quicantel."
"Sir."
Kashimir entered the conference room and looked for Jin.
"Lord Nodav Sarseong has come to Tichan."
Nodav Sarseong, that was Sandra Ziph's alias.
Jin was no longer surprised by her sudden move to visit Tichan openly during this sensitive time. She was a good person who did more for others.
"Did she come alone?"
"No."
Jin naturally thought she would have come to Tichan with Hedo, but Sandra's companion was someone else.
"Veradin Ziph, he came with her."
Jin's pupils grew larger.
He had worried whether he would be able to meet him once before leaving for Lafrarosa.
The meeting with his unfortunate friend depended entirely on Ziph's judgment, not his own.
"Even though we've basically entered a ceasefire, it's quite a move to send the two of them without any escort. Ziph must be feeling desperate."
Jin immediately recognized the intentions of Ziph's decision-makers, given the fact that the two of them had no separate escorts like Hedo.
"Yes, in my opinion, they seem to be trying to dig up some information using the relationship between the two of them and you."
"Let's meet them right away."
